text.en: Kirby, The War Against Japan, vol. I, p. 362: after the withdrawal to the island the Singapore garrison was about 85,000 men, including some 15,000 base, administrative and non-combatant troops.
text.zh: Kirby《对日战争》第一卷第 362 页：撤到岛上之后，新加坡守军约 85,000 人，其中约 15,000 人是后勤、行政和非战斗人员。

text.en: Lim Tin Seng, 'From Exclusive to Inclusive Remembrance: The Civilian War Memorial', BiblioAsia 7(2), Jul 2011 (National Library Board): 'The Japanese put the figure at about 5,000, while the Chinese estimated it to be around 100,000. But it has been widely assumed that the number of victims was between 25,000 and 50,000.' After the operation the Chinese community had to raise $50 million as 'tribute money'. In February 1962 a mass grave was unearthed at Siglap; the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce searched for others and demanded a 'blood debt' from Japan. The Civilian War Memorial was unveiled on 15 February 1967, and a commemorative service is held there every 15 February.
text.zh: 林振胜《从排他到包容的纪念：日据时期死难人民纪念碑》，《BiblioAsia》第 7 卷第 2 期（2011 年 7 月，新加坡国家图书馆管理局）：“日方估计约 5,000 人，华人估计约 10 万人。但一般认为遇难者在 25,000 至 50,000 人之间。”行动之后，华人社会被迫筹集 5,000 万元“奉纳金”。1962 年 2 月实里达（Siglap）发现集体坟场；中华总商会寻找其他坟场，并向日本要求偿还“血债”。纪念碑于 1967 年 2 月 15 日揭幕，此后每年 2 月 15 日在碑前举行纪念仪式。

text.en: Wai Keng Kwok, Justice Done? Criminal and Moral Responsibility Issues in the Chinese Massacres Trial, Singapore, 1947 (Yale University Genocide Studies Program, Working Paper 18, 2001): Chinese 'males aged eighteen to fifty should present themselves for inspection'; 'officially, the "Chinese Massacres" Trial of March 1947 puts the number at around five thousand but unofficially … as high as fifty thousand'.
text.zh: Wai Keng Kwok《正义得到伸张了吗？1947 年新加坡“华侨大屠杀”审判中的刑事与道德责任问题》（耶鲁大学种族灭绝研究项目工作论文第 18 号，2001）：“18 岁至 50 岁的华人男子须前往接受检查”；“1947 年 3 月的‘华侨大屠杀’审判官方认定的人数约为 5,000，但非官方的估计……高达 5 万”。

text.en: Hayashi Hirofumi (Kanto Gakuin University), 'Massacre of Chinese in Singapore and its Coverage in Postwar Japan': mass screening was carried out mainly by Kempeitai personnel between 21 and 23 February 1942 in the urban areas and by the Imperial Guard Division at the end of February in the suburbs; those picked out were taken to the coast and machine-gunned. The diary of the Kempeitai commander Kawamura Saburō gives 5,000 killed; a 25th Army intelligence record of 28 May 1942 gives 11,110 'missing as a result of bombing and the purge'.
text.zh: 林博史（关东学院大学）《新加坡华侨大屠杀及其在战后日本的报道》：大检证在市区主要由宪兵队于 1942 年 2 月 21 日至 23 日进行，郊区由近卫师团在 2 月底进行；被挑出的人被押到海边用机枪扫射。宪兵队指挥官河村参郎的日记记为 5,000 人；第 25 军 1942 年 5 月 28 日的情报记录记为“因轰炸和肃清而失踪”11,110 人。

note.en: Hayashi notes that the credibility of the 11,110 figure is open to question; he regards the real number as considerably higher than the Japanese records.
note.zh: 林博史指出 11,110 这个数字的可信度存疑；日方记录普遍低于实际人数。

text.en: Roots.sg (National Heritage Board), historic site marker 'Changi Beach Massacre': 66 Chinese male civilians were killed by Japanese hojo kempei (auxiliary military police) firing squads at the water's edge on Changi Beach on 20 February 1942, during the Sook Ching operation (18 February – 4 March 1942).
text.zh: Roots.sg（新加坡国家文物局）史迹标志“樟宜海滩屠杀”：1942 年 2 月 20 日，66 名华人男性平民在樟宜海滩水边被日本辅助宪兵行刑队枪杀；这是肃清行动（1942 年 2 月 18 日至 3 月 4 日）的一部分。

text.en: Roots.sg (National Heritage Board), historic site marker 'Punggol Beach Massacre': on 28 February 1942 some 400 Chinese civilians, victims of the Sook Ching purge, were killed by the Japanese on this north-eastern shore.
text.zh: Roots.sg（新加坡国家文物局）史迹标志“榜鹅海滩屠杀”：1942 年 2 月 28 日，约 400 名华人平民在这片东北海岸被日军杀害，他们是肃清行动的受害者。

text.en: SG101 (Government of Singapore), 'Punggol Beach: an Operation Sook Ching site': from 21 February to 4 March 1942 Chinese males between the ages of 18 and 50 were summoned to mass screening centres; those identified as anti-Japanese were taken away and killed.
text.zh: SG101（新加坡政府）《榜鹅海滩：肃清行动地点》：1942 年 2 月 21 日至 3 月 4 日，18 至 50 岁的华人男子被召集到各大检证中心；被认定为“抗日分子”的人被带走杀害。

text.en: Timothy Pwee, 'A War Crimes Trial Snapshot', BiblioAsia, 1 January 2016 (National Library Board): 131 war-crimes trials were held in Singapore between 21 January 1946 and 12 March 1948; the 'Double Tenth' trial (18 March – 15 April 1946) involved 21 Japanese soldiers and interpreters accused of torturing and killing internees of Changi Prison, where the Kempeitai had raided on 10 October 1943 and found a wireless set, after which 57 internees were tortured and interrogated over several months and 15 died; the main Sook Ching trial, at the Victoria Memorial Hall from 10 March to 2 April 1947, found all seven accused officers guilty — Lieutenant-General Kawamura Saburō and Lieutenant-Colonel Oishi Masayuki were sentenced to death and the other five to life imprisonment; the figure most often quoted for the Sook Ching comes from an affidavit by Lieutenant-Colonel Hishakari Takafumi, then a newspaper correspondent, that the plan was to kill 50,000 Chinese and half that number had been reached when the order came to stop.
text.zh: Timothy Pwee《战犯审判掠影》，《BiblioAsia》2016 年 1 月 1 日（新加坡国家图书馆管理局）：1946 年 1 月 21 日至 1948 年 3 月 12 日，新加坡共举行 131 场战犯审判；“双十”审判（1946 年 3 月 18 日至 4 月 15 日）的被告是 21 名日本军人和翻译，罪名是拷打和杀害樟宜监狱的被拘留者——1943 年 10 月 10 日宪兵队搜查监狱、搜出一台无线电，此后 57 名被拘留者在几个月里受到拷打审讯，15 人死亡；肃清案的主审判 1947 年 3 月 10 日至 4 月 2 日在维多利亚纪念堂举行，七名被告军官全部有罪，河村参郎中将和大石正幸中佐被判死刑，其余五人终身监禁；关于肃清人数，最常被引用的是当时任报社记者的Hishakari Takafumi 中佐的宣誓书：计划杀 5 万名华人，杀到一半时接到停止的命令。
